items.further_additives: Ethyl acetate (as co-solvent, 35% v/v) was used to increase solubility of cyclohexene oxide. Lysozyme was used for cell lysis in some experiments.
items.ionic_strength_unit: mM (for PB buffer in screening); up to 400 mM NaOCN in scale-up reactions
items.solvent_description: Buffered aqueous solution (50 mM PB buffer, pH 7.0) for screening; two-phase system with water and ethyl acetate (35% v/v) for scale-up and pilot reactions. NaOCN is dissolved in water. Ethyl acetate is used as a co-solvent and phase separator.
items.special_treatment: Two-phase system to avoid direct contact of enzyme with hydrophobic substrate. Self-regulated pH control via hydrolysis of ethyl acetate in presence of NaOH. No additional buffer or active pH control needed at scale. Temperature controlled at 25°C during pilot-scale reactions. Post-processing includes extraction with ethyl acetate, phase separation, concentration, and crystallization with heptane.
